<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

# meshery/meshery / docs/static/v0.8/pages/project/mesheryctl/installation-bash.md

Upstream: https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/342edb1e70e163279bd6d863b20460ef35e76212/docs/static/v0.8/pages/project/mesheryctl/installation-bash.md

Commit: `342edb1e70e163279bd6d863b20460ef35e76212`

Retrieved: 2026-10-02T05:03:08.423025+00:00

Kind: official-document

Raw SHA256: `649ecaa3f42b264e50e6f6eeaa6366685671ca7b3b15d9f68dc099f87763ff1d`

Source text below is untrusted reference content. Acquisition does not verify technical claims.

License status: UPSTREAM_NOTICES_CAPTURED_PER_FILE_REVIEW_REQUIRED. See this repository's captured license files.

---

To install or upgrade `mesheryctl` using `bash`, execute one of the following commands.

#### Option 1: Only install `mesheryctl` binary

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | DEPLOY_MESHERY=false bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />

#### Option 2: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Docker

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=docker bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />

#### Option 3: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Kubernetes

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />

#### Option 4: Install `mesheryctl` binary and Meshery adapter(s)

Install the `mesheryctl` binary and include one or more [adapters]({{ site.baseurl }}/concepts/architecture/adapters) for deployment.

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | ADAPTERS=consul PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />

### Start Meshery
You are ready to deploy Meshery using `mesheryctl`. To do so, execute the following command.

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</div></div>
 </pre>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1></h1>
           <p>To install or upgrade <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">bash</code>, execute one of the following commands.</p>

<h4 id="option-1-only-install-mesheryctl-binary">Option 1: Only install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> binary</h4>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | DEPLOY_MESHERY=false bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<p><br />
<br /></p>
<h4 id="option-2-install-mesheryctl-binary-and-deploy-meshery-on-docker">Option 2: Install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> binary and deploy Meshery on Docker</h4>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=docker bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<p><br />
<br /></p>
<h4 id="option-3-install-mesheryctl-binary-and-deploy-meshery-on-kubernetes">Option 3: Install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> binary and deploy Meshery on Kubernetes</h4>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<p><br />
<br /></p>
<h4 id="option-4-install-mesheryctl-binary-and-meshery-adapters">Option 4: Install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> binary and Meshery adapter(s)</h4>

<p>Install the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> binary and include one or more <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">adapters</a> for deployment.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | ADAPTERS=consul PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<p><br />
<br /></p>
<h3 id="start-meshery">Start Meshery</h3>
<p>You are ready to deploy Meshery using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>. To do so, execute the following command.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</div></div>
 </pre>


<script>
  /*clipboard.js code*/
</script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

# meshery/meshery / docs/static/v0.8/pages/project/mesheryctl/installation-brew.md

Upstream: https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/342edb1e70e163279bd6d863b20460ef35e76212/docs/static/v0.8/pages/project/mesheryctl/installation-brew.md

### Prerequisites

You need to have `Brew` installed on your **Linux** or **macOS** system to perform these actions.

### Install `mesheryctl` using Brew

To install `mesheryctl` using Homebrew, execute the following command.

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew install mesheryctl
 </div></div>
</pre>

You're ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command.

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>

Meshery Server supports customizing the authentication flow callback URL, which can be configured in the following way.

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>

`mesheryctl` uses your current Kubernetes context (the `KUBECONFIG` environment variable; `~/.kube/config` by default). Confirm that this is the Kubernetes cluster you want Meshery to interact with by running: `kubectl config get-contexts`.

If there are multiple contexts in your kubeconfig file, specify the one you want to use with the `use-context` subcommand: `kubectl config use-context <context-to-use>`.

### Upgrade `mesheryctl` using Brew

To upgrade `mesheryctl`, execute the following command.

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew upgrade mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>

</summary>

          <h1>Prerequisites</h1>
           <h3 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites</h3>

<p>You need to have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Brew</code> installed on your <strong>Linux</strong> or <strong>macOS</strong> system to perform these actions.</p>

<h3 id="install-mesheryctl-using-brew">Install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> using Brew</h3>

<p>To install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> using Homebrew, execute the following command.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew install mesheryctl
 </div></div>
</pre>

<p>You’re ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>

<p>Meshery Server supports customizing the authentication flow callback URL, which can be configured in the following way.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> uses your current Kubernetes context (the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">KUBECONFIG</code> environment variable; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">~/.kube/config</code> by default). Confirm that this is the Kubernetes cluster you want Meshery to interact with by running: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl config get-contexts</code>.</p>

<p>If there are multiple contexts in your kubeconfig file, specify the one you want to use with the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">use-context</code> subcommand: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl config use-context &lt;context-to-use&gt;</code>.</p>

<h3 id="upgrade-mesheryctl-using-brew">Upgrade <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> using Brew</h3>

<p>To upgrade <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>, execute the following command.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew upgrade mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<details>
<summary>
Example output of a successful upgrade.
</summary>

<pre><code>
➜  ~ brew upgrade mesheryctl
==&gt; Upgrading 1 outdated package:
meshery/tap/mesheryctl 0.3.2 -&gt; 0.3.4
==&gt; Upgrading meshery/tap/mesheryctl
==&gt; Downloading https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/download/v0.3.4/mesheryctl_0.3.4_Darwin_x86_64.zip
==&gt; Downloading from https://github-production-release-asset-2e65be.s3.amazonaws.com/157554479/17522b00-2af0-11ea-8aef-cbfe8
######################################################################## 100.0%
🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/mesheryctl/0.3.4: 5 files, 10.2MB, built in 4 seconds
Removing: /usr/local/Cellar/mesheryctl/0.3.2... (5 files, 10.2MB)
Removing: /Users/lee/Library/Caches/Homebrew/mesheryctl--0.3.2.zip... (3.9MB)
==&gt; Checking for dependents of upgraded formulae...
==&gt; No dependents found!
</code></pre>
<br />
</details>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

## Prerequisites

You need to have `scoop` installed on your Windows system to perform these actions.

### Install `mesheryctl` with Scoop

To install `mesheryctl` using Scoop, execute the following commands.

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">scoop bucket add mesheryctl https://github.com/meshery/scoop-bucket.git
scoop install mesheryctl</div></div>
</pre>

You're ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command:

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</div></div>
</pre>

### Upgrade `mesheryctl` with Scoop

To upgrade `mesheryctl`, execute the following command.

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">scoop update mesheryctl</div></div>
</pre>

          <h1>Prerequisites</h1>
           <h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites</h2>

<p>You need to have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">scoop</code> installed on your Windows system to perform these actions.</p>

<h3 id="install-mesheryctl-with-scoop">Install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> with Scoop</h3>

<p>To install <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> using Scoop, execute the following commands.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">scoop bucket add mesheryctl https://github.com/meshery/scoop-bucket.git
scoop install mesheryctl</div></div>
</pre>

<p>You’re ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</div></div>
</pre>

<h3 id="upgrade-mesheryctl-with-scoop">Upgrade <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> with Scoop</h3>

<p>To upgrade <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>, execute the following command.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">scoop update mesheryctl</div></div>
</pre>


<script>
  /*clipboard.js code*/
</script>

  src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Community</h1>
           <p>Meshery is a CNCF project maintained by engineers from VMware, Red Hat, Rackspace, Citrix, Instabase, Microsoft, OpenGov, Computas AS, Rill Data, Quantex, Lumina Networks, API7, F5, Citi, Acquia, and HashiCorp. Meshery is an open source project that adheres to the <a href="https://github.com/cncf/foundation/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md">CNCF’s Code of Conduct</a>. Meshery advance the state of the art surrounding cloud native management and enable adopters of Cloud Native technologies and techniques to do so with confidence. Our shared commitment to the open source spirit pushes Meshery forward.</p>

<h2 id="getting-involved-in-the-community">Getting involved in the Community</h2>

<p>Get involved with Meshery and supporting projects. Start by reading through the <a href="https://meshery.io/community">Newcomers Guide</a>, which provides details on how to participate. Seek out other community members, who will make sure you are not left out. We always have a role for everyone whether to be a code-writer, a community manager, user, advocate, or just to listen in. The Meshery community is always open and warmly welcomes you.  If this is your first time making open source contribution, you are in the right place!</p>

<p>Please see our <a href="/v0.8/project/contributing">contributing guide</a> for specific details about setting up your development environment and to start learning the innerworkings of a specific Meshery component.</p>

<h4 id="community-first">Community First</h4>

<p>The Meshery project is community-built and welcomes collaboration! <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery"><i class="fab fa-github"></i> Fork Meshery</a></p>

<ul>
  <li>Join any of the <a href="https://meshery.io/calendar">community meetings</a>.</li>
  <li>Subscribe to the <a href="https://meshery.io/calendar">community calendar</a>.</li>
  <li>Fill-in a <a href="https://meshery.io/newcomers">community member form</a> to gain access to community resources.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="talking-about-meshery">Talking about Meshery?</h2>

<p>Giving a talk or hosting a meetup about Meshery? Leverage existing slides or request swag to support your talk.</p>

<div class="wrapper">
    <a href="https://forms.gle/1jqY7HWveSFKCdnD6"><div class="overview">Share your event</div></a>
    <a href="https://meshery.io/newcomers"><div class="overview">Access slides and resources</div></a>
</div>

<script src="https://stackpath.bootstrapcdn.com/bootstrap/4.1.3/js/bootstrap.min.js" integrity="sha384-ChfqqxuZUCnJSK3+MXmPNIyE6ZbWh2IMqE241rYiqJxyMiZ6OW/JmZQ5stwEULTy" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script
  src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

  crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Build & Release (CI)</h1>
           <p>Meshery’s build and release system incorporates many tools, organized into different workflows each triggered by different events. Meshery’s build and release system does not run on a schedule, but is event-driven. GitHub Actions are used to define Meshery’s CI workflows. New builds of Meshery and its various components are automatically generated upon push, release, and other similar events, typically in relation to their respective master branches.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Meshery Test Documents</h4>
 The Meshery Test Strategy (<a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/11nAxYtz2SUusCYZ0JeNRrOLIxkgmmbUVWz63MBZV2oE/edit">1</a>,<a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/14vbwnKafqxrr-cJOmLWEvvj75MFrxFKiUdfPwZRhg64/edit">2</a>) is a comprehensive document that outlines the approach to testing, types of tests, frameworks used - test strategy - for each of Meshery's architectural components. The <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13Ir4gfaKoAX9r8qYjAFFl_U9ntke4X5ndREY1T7bnVs/edit">Meshery Test Plan</a> is a tactical spreadsheet that *itemizes* specific integration and end-to-end test cases and tracks their status. It includes a list of GitHub workflows and their purpose. Join the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GrVdGHZAYeu6wHNLLoiaKNqBtk7enXE9XeDRCvdA4bY/edit#">Meshery CI meeting</a> and/or the <a href="https://meshery.io/subscribe">developers mailing list</a> to get involved.
</div>

<h2 id="artifacts">Artifacts</h2>

<p>Today, Meshery and Meshery adapters are released as Docker container images, available on Docker Hub. Meshery adapters are out-of-process adapters (meaning not compiled into the main Meshery binary), and as such, are independent build artifacts and Helm charts. The Docker images are created and tagged with the git commit SHA, then pushed to Docker Hub automatically using GitHub Actions. Subsequently, when contributions containing content for the Helm charts of Meshery and Meshery Adapter are linted and merged, they will be pushed and released to <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery.io">meshery.io</a> Github page by GitHub Action automatically.</p>

<p>All repositories under the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">github.com/meshery</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">github.com/meshery-extensions</code> organizations use immutable releases.
<img width="954" height="166" alt="immutable-releases-setting" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4435086f-db09-449e-a154-70979b8b01d1" /></p>

<h3 id="artifact-repositories">Artifact Repositories</h3>

<p>Artifacts produced in the build processes are published and persisted in different public repositories and in different formats.</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Location</th>
      <th>Project</th>
      <th>Repository</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Docker Hub</td>
      <td>Meshery</td>
      <td><a href="https://hub.docker.com/r/meshery/meshery">https://hub.docker.com/r/meshery/meshery</a></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>GitHub</td>
      <td>mesheryctl</td>
      <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases">https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases</a></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Docker Hub</td>
      <td>Meshery Adapter for &lt;adapter-name&gt;</td>
      <td>https://hub.docker.com/r/meshery/meshery-&lt;adapter-name&gt;&gt;</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Docs</td>
      <td>Meshery Documentation</td>
      <td><a href="https://docs.meshery.io">https://docs.meshery.io</a></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>GitHub</td>
      <td><a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a></td>
      <td><a href="https://github.com/service-mesh-performance/service-mesh-performance">https://github.com/service-mesh-performance</a></td>
    </tr>

      <td>Github</td>

      <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery.io/tree/master/charts">https://github.com/meshery/meshery.io/tree/master/charts</a></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<h2 id="secrets">Secrets</h2>

<p>Some portions of the workflow require secrets to accomplish their tasks. These secrets are defined within the respective repositories and accessible to workflows during runtime. Currently defined secrets include:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DOCKER_USERNAME</code>: Username of the Docker Hub user with the right privileges to push images</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DOCKER_PASSWORD</code>: Password for the Docker Hub user</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">IMAGE_NAME</code>: appropriate image name for each of the Docker container images. All are under the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery</code> org.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SLACK_BOT_TOKEN</code>: Used for notification of new GitHub stars given to the Meshery repo.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">GLOBAL_TOKEN</code>: Used for securely transmitting performance test results for the None Provider.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NPM_TOKEN</code>: npm authentication token, used to perform authentication against the npm registry in meshery deployment workflow.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">GH_ACCESS_TOKEN</code>: GitHub access token for various operations</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">INTEGRATION_SPREADSHEET_CRED</code>: Credentials for integration spreadsheet access</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MAIL_PASSWORD</code>: Password for email notifications</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MAIL_USERNAME</code>: Username for email notifications</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MESHERY_PROVIDER_TOKEN</code>: Token for Meshery provider authentication</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MESHERY_TOKEN</code>: General Meshery authentication token</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">METAL_AUTH_TOKEN</code>: Authentication token for metal provider</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">METAL_SERVER1</code>: Configuration for metal server 1</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN</code>: Authentication token for Netlify</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NETLIFY_SITE_ID</code>: Site ID for Netlify deployments</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PLAYGROUND_CONFIG</code>: Configuration for playground environments</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER_TOKEN</code>: General provider authentication token</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RELEASEDRAFTER_PAT</code>: Personal access token for Release Drafter</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RELEASEDRAFTER_PAT</code>: Personal access token for release notes generation</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_EMAIL</code>: Email used for authentication in Playwright tests</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_PASS</code>: Password used for authentication in Playwright tests</li>
</ul>

<p>The Docker Hub user, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryci</code>, belongs to the “ciusers” team in Docker Hub and acts as the service account under which these automated builds are being pushed. Every time a new Docker Hub repository is created we have to grant “Admin” (in order to update the README in the Docker Hub repository) permissions to the ciusers team.</p>

<h2 id="checks-and-tests">Checks and Tests</h2>

<p>Meshery’s CI workflow incorporates several checks (partial list below) during merges and/or commits to any branches and pull requests to master branch to prevent broken code from being merged into master.</p>

<p>Collectively, Meshery repositories will generally have CI workflow for commits and pull requests that consist of the following actions:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Lint check (golint)</li>
  <li>Static analysis check (staticcheck)</li>
  <li>Vet (govet)</li>
  <li>Security checks (gosec)</li>
  <li>Unit tests (go tests)</li>
  <li>Build (go build)</li>
  <li>Release binaries through GoReleaser (only for mesheryctl in the Meshery repository)</li>
  <li>Docker build, tag and push</li>
  <li>Helm charts lint (helm)</li>
  <li>Helm charts release, tag and push(stefanprodan/helm-gh-pages@master)</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="ui-build-system">UI Build System</h3>

<p>Meshery UI (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/ui</code>) and Provider UI (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/provider-ui</code>) are built using <a href="https://nextjs.org/">Next.js</a> with <a href="https://swc.rs/">SWC</a> (Speedy Web Compiler) as the default compiler.</p>

<p><strong>Build Commands</strong>:</p>
<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make ui-build</code> - Builds both Meshery UI and Provider UI</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make ui-provider-build</code> - Builds Provider UI only</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="tests-for-adapters">Tests for adapters</h2>

<p>All Meshery adapters use a central workflow that is referenced in each of their test workflows which get triggered every time a pull request is made. These
tests in adapters are end-to-end tests and use patternfile. The reusable workflow is present in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.github/workflows</code> in Meshery repository with the workflow name “Test for Meshery adapters using patternfile”</p>

<h3 id="pre-requisite-for-referencing-this-workflow">Pre-requisite for referencing this workflow</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Using actions/upload-artifact@v2 a patternfile has to be uploaded as an artifact with the name as “patternfile”.</li>
  <li>The name of the uploaded patterfile should be passed in</li>
</ol>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  ...
  with:
      patternfile_name: &lt; name of the patternfile which is uploaded &gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<ol>
  <li>Note: This Job is pre-run to the actual test. This is done in order to create patternfiles dynamically and use them. Therefore name of this jobs has to be passed as</li>
</ol>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  ...
  needs:
     &lt; Name of the pre-requisite job &gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<ol>
  <li>There should be an infinite token passed in: (Or else local provider will be used)</li>
</ol>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  ...
  secrets:
    token: $
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="functionality-of-central-workflow">Functionality of Central Workflow</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Checks out the code of the repository(on the ref of latest commit of branch which made the PR) in which it is referenced.</li>
  <li>Starts a minikube cluster</li>
  <li>Builds a docker image of the adapter and sets minikube to use docker’s registry.</li>
  <li>Starts the adapter and Meshery Server (The url to deployment and service yaml of adapter are configurable).
NOTE: The adapter name has to passed in:</li>
</ol>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  ...
  with:
     adapter_name: &lt; NAME OF THE ADAPTER &gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<ol>
  <li>The uploaded patternfile is deployed.</li>
  <li>Workflow sleeps for some time.</li>
  <li>Then the assertion is made that the pods passed in-</li>
</ol>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  ...
  with:
     expected_pods: &lt; pod1,pod2,pod3 &gt;  #comma separated pod names that will be expected to be present after patternfile is deployed
</code></pre></div></div>

<ol>
  <li>And these pods are present in their respective namespaces passed in-</li>
</ol>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  ...
  with:
     expected_pods_namespaces: &lt; pod1ns, pod2ns , pod3ns &gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="expected-inputs-of-this-workflow">Expected inputs of this workflow</h3>

<hr />

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>inputs:
  expected_pods:
    required: true
    type: string
  expected_pods_namespaces:
    required: true
    type: string
  service_url:
    required: true
    type: string
  deployment_url:
    required: true
    type: string
  adapter_name:
    required: true
    type: string
  patternfile_name:
    required: true
    type: string
  provider:
    required: false
    type: string
secrets:
  token:
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="expected-outputs-of-this-workflow">Expected outputs of this workflow</h3>

<p>The pods passed in “expected_pods” are running in the subsequent namespaces passed in “expected_pods_namespaces”. If not, the workflow fails</p>

<h2 id="automated-builds">Automated Builds</h2>

<p>All Meshery GitHub repositories are configured with GitHub Actions. Everytime a pull request is submitted against the master branch of any repository, that repository’s GitHub Actions will be invoked (whether the PR is merged or not). Workflows defined in Meshery repository will generally (but not always) perform the following actions:</p>

<ol>
  <li>trigger a Docker build to build a Docker container image</li>
  <li>generate two Docker tags:
    <ol>
      <li>a tag containing the git merge SHA</li>
      <li>a tag containing that particular release’s git tag (if one is present)</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
  <li>assign each of these two tags to the new container image as well as the latest tag.</li>
  <li>push the new Docker tags and image to Docker Hub.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="mesheryctl"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code></h3>

<p>As a special case, the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery</code> repository contains an additional artifact produced during each build. This artifact is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>, which is built as an executable binary. In order to make the job of building <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> easier for a combination of different platform architectures and operating systems, we are using <a href="https://goreleaser.com">GoReleaser</a>. Irrespective of branch, for every git commit and git push to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery</code> repository, GoReleaser will execute and generate the OS and arch-specific binaries (but will NOT persist these artifacts in GitHub). Even though mesheryctl binaries are built each time a pull request is merged to master, only stable channel artifacts are published (persisted).</p>

<h4 id="releasing-mesheryctl-to-github">Releasing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> to GitHub</h4>

<p>Only when a git tag containing a semantic version number is present (is a commit in the master branch) will GoReleaser execute, generate the archives, and also publish the archives to <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases">Meshery’s GitHub releases</a> automatically. GoReleaser is configured to generate artifacts for the following OS, ARCH combination:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Darwin - i386, x86_64</li>
  <li>Linux - i386, x86_64</li>
  <li>Windows - i386, x86_64</li>
  <li>FreeBSD - i386, x86_64</li>
</ul>

<p>The artifacts will be made available as a tar.gz archive for all the operating systems. mesheryctl is bundled into packages for commonly used package managers: homebrew and scoop.</p>

<h5 id="homebrew">Homebrew</h5>

<p>GoReleaser facilitates the creation of a brew formula for mesheryctl. The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/homebrew-tap">homebrew-tap</a> repository is the location for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>’s brew formulas. Releases of mesheryctl are  published in the official homebrew-core tap at https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pkgs/container/core%2Fmesheryctl.</p>

<h5 id="scoop">Scoop</h5>

<p>GoReleaser facilitates the creation of a Scoop app for mesheryctl. The <a href="https://github.com/meshkit/scoop-bucket">scoop-bucket</a> repository is the location of Meshery’s Scoop bucket.</p>

<h2 id="helm-charts-lint-check-build-and-release">Helm Charts Lint Check, Build, and Release</h2>

<p>The charts lint check, charts build, and charts release workflows are all triggered by GitHub events. Sometimes this event is the opening, updating, or merging of a branch, or sometimes a manual invocation, or a GitHub release event.</p>

<h3 id="check-helm-charts">Check Helm Charts</h3>

<p>Every PR which includes changes to the files under <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">install/kubernetes/</code> directory in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshery</code> will trigger a Github Action to check for any mistakes in Helm charts using the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">helm lint</code> command.</p>

<h3 id="release-helm-charts-to-github-and-artifact-hub">Release Helm Charts to Github and Artifact Hub</h3>

<p>New Meshery Helm charts are published upon trigger of a release event in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshery</code> repo. New versions of Meshery’s Helm charts are published to <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery.io/tree/master/charts">Meshery’s Helm charts release page</a>. [Artifact Hub] (https://artifacthub.io/packages/helm/meshery/meshery) syncs with these updated Meshery Helm charts.</p>

<h2 id="release-versioning">Release Versioning</h2>

<p>Meshery and its components follow the commonly used, semantic versioning for its release numbering scheme. Given a version number MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.BUILD, increment the:</p>

<ul>
  <li>MAJOR version - major changes with rare potential for incompatible API changes.</li>
  <li>MINOR version - add functionality in a backwards-compatible manner.</li>
  <li>PATCH version - mostly for bug and security fixes.</li>
  <li>AlPHA/BETA/RC - used to facilitate early testing of an upcoming release.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="component-versioning">Component Versioning</h3>

<p>Meshery comprises a number of components including a server, adapters, UI, and CLI. As an application, Meshery is a composition of these different functional components. While all of Meshery’s components generally deploy as a collective unit (together), each component is versioned independently, so as to allow them to be loosely coupled and iterate on functionality independently. Some of the components must be upgraded simultaneously, while others may be upgraded independently. See <a href="/v0.8/installation/upgrades">Upgrading Meshery</a> for more information.</p>

<p>GitHub release tags will contain a semantic version number. Semantic version numbers will have to be managed manually by tagging a relevant commit in the master branch with a semantic version number (example: v1.2.3).</p>

<h2 id="release-process">Release Process</h2>

<p>Documentation of Meshery releases contains a table of releases and release notes and should be updated with each release.</p>

<h1 id="meshery-release-documents-and-release-lead-responsibilities">Meshery Release Documents and Release Lead Responsibilities</h1>

<h2 id="meshery-release-documents">Meshery Release Documents</h2>

<p>Meshery uses several types of release documents to standardize the purpose, style, and structure of release information. These documents are crucial for maintaining clear communication about changes, updates, and new features in Meshery releases.</p>

<h3 id="types-of-release-documents">Types of Release Documents</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Changelogs</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Comprehensive list of all changes since the prior release</li>
      <li>Generated automatically by tools like ReleaseDrafter</li>
      <li>Contains detailed, technical information</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Release Notes</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Curated, bulleted list of highlights</li>
      <li>Summarized and categorized in human-readable format</li>
      <li>Includes some engineering terminology and issue references</li>
      <li>Based on ReleaseDrafter output, but human-summarized and refined</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Release Announcement</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Human-written summary highlighting significant items</li>
      <li>Includes caveats (e.g., incompatibility on upgrade)</li>
      <li>Provides links to other information sources (upgrade guide, feature blogs, full bug fix list)</li>
      <li>Contains graphics and links to in-depth documentation</li>
      <li>Distributed via #announcements Slack channel and public mailing list (for stable releases)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>User and Upgrade Docs</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>How-to guides for new features</li>
      <li>Updates to user-facing documentation</li>
      <li>Includes Upgrade Guide updates for version-to-version considerations</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Feature-functionality Blogs</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>In-depth reviews of new or significantly augmented functionality</li>
      <li>Explains the what, why, and how of new features</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2 id="meshery-release-lead-responsibilities">Meshery Release Lead Responsibilities</h2>

<p>The Meshery Release Lead plays a crucial role in coordinating and executing the release process. Their responsibilities span approximately 5 months per release cycle.</p>

<h3 id="pre-release-phase-1-month">Pre-Release Phase (1 month)</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Release Planning</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Schedule and organize release planning meetings</li>
      <li>Define and communicate release timelines</li>
      <li>Coordinate with development, testing, and documentation teams</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Feature Management</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Oversee feature implementation and prioritization</li>
      <li>Ensure all planned features are completed or properly deferred</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Quality Assurance</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Coordinate with QA team to ensure thorough testing</li>
      <li>Address and prioritize bug fixes</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Documentation Preparation</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Ensure all new features and changes are properly documented</li>
      <li>Oversee the creation and updating of release notes</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Release Build Preparation</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Manage the creation of release branches</li>
      <li>Oversee the release build process</li>
      <li>Coordinate with DevOps for deployment preparations</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="active-maintenance-phase-6-months">Active Maintenance Phase (6 months)</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ongoing Releases</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Manage minor releases every 3 weeks</li>
      <li>Coordinate vulnerability fix integrations</li>
      <li>Oversee cherry-pick decisions for backports</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Monitoring and Issue Resolution</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Monitor for release blockers</li>
      <li>Coordinate resolution of critical issues</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Communication</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Lead weekly Meshery build and release meetings</li>
      <li>Provide regular status updates to the community</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Documentation Updates</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Ensure documentation remains current throughout the maintenance phase</li>
      <li>Oversee updates to user guides and upgrade instructions</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>End-of-Life Procedures</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Manage the process for deprecating the release</li>
      <li>Ensure proper handover to the next release cycle</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="release-manager-qualifications-and-selection">Release Manager Qualifications and Selection</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Must be an active community member for at least 3 months</li>
  <li>Approved by majority vote of current maintainers</li>
  <li>At least one release manager must meet requirements for vulnerability-related access</li>
</ul>

<p>To volunteer as a Meshery Release Lead, interested individuals should contact a current maintainer or self-nominate.</p>

<p>This structured approach to release documentation and management ensures consistency, clarity, and efficiency in Meshery’s release process, facilitating better communication with users and smoother project development.</p>

<h3 id="automated-releases">Automated Releases</h3>

<p>Releases are manually triggered by a member of the release team publishing a release. Release names and release tags need to be assigned by the publishing team member. GitHub Action workflows will trigger and take care of running the required steps and publishing all artifacts (e.g., binary and docker images).</p>

<h3 id="workflow-triggers">Workflow Triggers</h3>

<p>The following events will trigger one or more workflows:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Tagged Release</li>
  <li>Commit pushed to the master branch</li>
  <li>PR opened or commit pushed to PR branch</li>
  <li>PR merged to the master branch</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="release-notes">Release Notes</h3>

<p>While use of GitHub Actions facilitates automated builds, ReleaseDrafter is helping with facilitating automated release notes and versioning.</p>

<h3 id="generating-release-notes">Generating Release Notes</h3>

<p>ReleaseDrafter generates a GitHub tag and release draft. ReleaseDrafter action will trigger and will automatically draft release notes according to the configuration set-up. ReleaseDrafter drafts releases as soon as a commit is made into master after the previous release. The GitHub Action, ReleaseDrafter, is compatible with semantic releases and is used to auto-increment the semantic version number by looking at the previous release version.</p>

<h4 id="automated-release-notes-publishing">Automated Release Notes Publishing</h4>

<p>The publishing of release notes to Meshery Docs is automated. Triggered by a release event, a workflow will checkout the Meshery repo, copy the auto-drafted release notes into a Jekyll collection in Meshery Docs, and generate a pull request.</p>

<h4 id="automated-release-notes-sending">Automated Release Notes Sending</h4>

<p>The sending of release notes is now automated as a step in the stable release channel workflow. The release notes are automatically sent to the <a href="https://groups.google.com/a/meshery.io/g/developers">developers@meshery.io mailing list</a>.</p>

<h4 id="automated-pull-request-labeler">Automated Pull Request Labeler</h4>

<p>A GitHub Issue labeler bot is configured to automatically assign labels to issues based on which files have changed in which directories. For example, a pull request with changes to files in the “/docs/**” folder will receive the “area/docs” label. Presence of the “area/docs” label is used to trigger documentation builds and Netlify builds of the Meshery Docs. Similar labels are assigned and used to trigger workflows or used as conditional flags in workflows to determine which workflows or which steps in a workflows to run.</p>

<h2 id="release-channels">Release Channels</h2>

<p>Artifacts of the builds for Meshery and its components are published under two different release channels, so that improved controls may be provided to both Meshery users and Meshery developers. The two release channels are <em>edge</em> and <em>stable</em> release channels.</p>

<p>Relative to stable releases, edge releases occur much more frequently. Edge releases are made with each merge to master, unless that merge to master is for a stable release. Stable releases are made with each merge to master when a GitHub release tag is also present in the workflow.</p>

<h3 id="stable-channel">Stable Channel</h3>

<p>The following is an example of the release channels and the docker tags used to differentiate them. The latest tag will be applied only to images in the stable release channel. Here are two releases with two different images.</p>

<p><strong>Latest Stable Image</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>meshery/meshery:stable-latest</li>
  <li>meshery/meshery:stable-v0.4.1</li>
  <li>meshery/meshery:stable-324vdgb (sha)</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Older Stable Image</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>meshery/meshery:stable-v0.4.0</li>
  <li>meshery/meshery:stable-289d02 (sha)</li>
</ul>

<p>Every docker image built receives either the edge tags or the stable tags. Which set of image tags assigned is determined by whether a release tag is present or not. In other words, stable channel docker images get the “stable” tags only in the presence of a release tag (e.g. v0.4.1).</p>

<h3 id="edge-channel">Edge Channel</h3>

<p>The Edge release channel provides early access to the latest features, allowing experimentation and feedback. Recent updates introduce dynamic versioning for Edge releases and improve compatibility with remote providers, ensuring a seamless experience. This makes the Edge channel valuable for users seeking cutting-edge features while contributing to the Meshery project. Docker image tags remain consistent for differentiation.</p>

<p>Stable and edge releases are both published to the same Docker Hub repository. Docker Hub repositories differentiate release channels by image tag. The following Docker images tagging convention is followed:</p>

<p><strong>Latest Edge Image</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>meshery/meshery:edge-latest</li>
  <li>meshery/meshery:edge-289d02 (sha)</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Older Edge Image</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>meshery/meshery:edge-324vdgb (sha)</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="switching-between-meshery-release-channels">Switching Between Meshery Release Channels</h3>

<p>Users are empowered to switch between release channels at their leisure.</p>

<h4 id="switching-release-channels-using-mesheryctl">Switching Release Channels Using mesheryctl</h4>

<p>Users can use mesheryctl to switch between release channels, e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system channel [stable|edge]</code>. Alternatively, users can manually switch between channels by updating the docker image tags in their meshery.yaml / Kubernetes manifest files. This command generates a meshery.yml (a docker-compose file) with release channel-appropriate tags for the different Docker container images.</p>

<h4 id="viewing-release-channel-and-version-information-in-meshery-ui">Viewing Release Channel and Version Information in Meshery UI</h4>

<p>Users are shown their Meshery deployment’s release channel subscription enient new setting in the Preferences area of the Meshery UI, so that people can alternatively use the UI to switch between channels if they like. Version numbers for Meshery adapters are also shown in the UI.</p>

<h2 id="release-cadence">Release Cadence</h2>

<p>Minor releases of the Meshery project are release frequently (on a monthly basis on average) with patch releases made on-demand in-between those times. The project does not have long term releases that are sustained with bug fixes, yet. Bug fixes and patches will be released as needed on the latest release version.</p>

<h3 id="release-support">Release Support</h3>

<p>General community support is available. Separately, third parties and partners may offer longer-term support solutions.</p>

<h4 id="pre-v10">Pre v1.0</h4>

<p>Project focuses on functionality, quality and adoption, while retaining the flexibility for shifts in architecture.</p>

<h4 id="post-v10">Post v1.0</h4>

<p>Once a 1.0 release has been made, Around once a month or so, the project maintainers will take one of these daily builds and run it through a number of additional qualification tests and tag the build as a Stable release. Around once a quarter or so, the project maintainers take one of these Stable releases, run through a bunch more tests and tag the build as a Long Term Support (LTS) release. Finally, if we find something wrong with an LTS release, we issue patches.</p>

<p>The different types (Daily, Stable, LTS) represent different product quality levels and different levels of support from the Meshery team. In this context, support means that we will produce patch releases for critical issues and offer technical assistance.</p>

<h2 id="versioning-documentation">Versioning Documentation</h2>

<h3 id="for-new-major-release">For new major release</h3>

<p>The structure which the docs follow right now is, The main <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">docs</code> folder has the most recent version of documentation, while there are sub-folders for previous versions, v0.x (x being the last major release).
On release of a new major version, the static html files for the most recent version is generated and is renamed as the release version (v0.x).</p>

<h5 id="steps">Steps:</h5>

<p>After cloning the Meshery repository</p>

<ol>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">cd docs</code> &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">bundle install</code> &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make docs</code></li>
  <li>On executing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make docs</code> a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">_site</code> folder is created which has static html files.</li>
  <li>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">_site</code> folder is renamed to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">v0.x</code>.</li>
  <li>This <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">v0.x</code> folder is now the latest version of docs.</li>
</ol>

<h5 id="in-the-v0x-folder"><em>In the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">v0.x</code> folder</em></h5>

<ol>
  <li>Search and replace all the instances where there is a direct path is defined to include the version name in the path, i.e, all paths to intra-page links and images should start with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/v0.x/</code>.</li>
</ol>

<ul>
  <li>Look for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">href="/</code> and replace with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">href="/0.x/</code></li>
  <li>Look for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">src="/</code>and replace with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">src="/0.x/</code> <br /><br />
<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/versioning-guide/search-and-replace.png">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/versioning-guide/search-and-replace.png" />
</a></li>
</ul>

<h3 id="for-old-release">For old release</h3>

<p>For older releases we have to travel back in time. Using the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Tags</code> in github we go to a previous release, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">v0.X.x</code>, the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.x</code> here should be the latest version of the archived docs.</p>

<h5 id="steps-1">Steps:</h5>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Copy the commit ID for that release. <br /><br />
<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/versioning-guide/commit-ID.png">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/versioning-guide/commit-ID.png" />
</a></p>
  </li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git checkout &lt;commit ID&gt;</code> &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">cd docs</code> &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">bundle install</code> &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make docs</code></li>
  <li>On executing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make docs</code> a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">_site</code> folder is created which has static html files.</li>
  <li>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">_site</code> folder is renamed to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">v0.X</code> and is copied into the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">docs</code> folder of the present version.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="bi-weekly-meetings">Bi-Weekly Meetings</h2>

<p>If you are passionate about CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, automated testing, managing deployments, or if you want to learn how to use Meshery and its features, you are invited to join the bi-weekly Build and Release meetings. Find meeting details and agenda in the <a href="https://meshery.io/calendar">community calendar</a> and the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GrVdGHZAYeu6wHNLLoiaKNqBtk7enXE9XeDRCvdA4bY/edit#">meeting minutes document</a>. The meetings are open to everyone and recorded for later viewing. We hope to see you there!</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Contributing to Meshery Adapters</h1>
           <p>Meshery Adapters are the Extension Points in Meshery’s architecture. Their design, the process of creating a new adapter is documented in <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters">Extensibility: Meshery Adapters</a>.</p>

<p>With the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#adapter">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> in mind, understand that development follows the usual fork-and-pull request workflow described here, see also GitHub Process. On forking GitHub deactivates all workflows. It is safe and good practice to activate them such that the code is validated on each push. This requires that branches filter for “on push” is set to ‘**’ to be triggered also on branches containing ‘/’  in their name.  The actions are parameterized using secrets (see Build &amp; Release Strategy). The Docker image is only built and pushed to Docker Hub if a tag is pushed and the corresponding authentication information is configured.</p>

<p>Each commit has to be signed off, see <a href="/v0.8/project/contributing">Contributing Overview</a>.</p>

<h3 id="running-an-adapter-as-a-container">Running an adapter as a container</h3>

<p>Testing your local changes running as a container can be accomplished in two ways:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Define the adapter’s address in the UI: Unless the running container is named as specified in the docker-run target in the Makefile, the container has to be removed manually first. Then, run <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make docker</code> followed by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make docker-run</code>. Then, connect to the adapter in the UI in “Settings &gt; Adapters” using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">localhost:&lt;port&gt;</code> if the meshery server is running as a binary, or <docker IP="" address="">:<port> if it is running as a docker container.</port></docker></li>
  <li>Using mesheryctl: In <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">~/.meshery/meshery.yaml</code>, change the tag specifying the image of the adapter to “latest”. Run make docker, followed by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start --skip-update</code>. This assumes mesheryctl system start has been executed at least once before.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="running-an-adapter-as-a-process">Running an adapter as a process</h3>

<p>Another way to test your local changes is to run the adapter as a process. To do this, clone the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshery</code> repository, and start Meshery Server using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make server</code>. Start the adapter from your IDE, or by executing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make run</code>. Then, in Meshery UI, add the adapter using “localhost:<PORT>”.</PORT></p>

<h3 id="creating-a-new-meshery-adapter">Creating a new Meshery Adapter</h3>

<p>Meshery uses adapters to manage and interact with different cloud native infrastructure. Meshery adapters are written in Go. Whether you are creating a new adapter or modifying an existing adapter, be sure to read the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b8JAMzr3Rntu7CudRaYv6r6ccACJONAB5t7ISCaPNuA/edit#">Meshery Adapters</a> design specification. For new adapters, start with the Repository Template(https://github.com/meshery/meshery).</p>

<ol>
  <li>Get the proto buf spec file from Meshery repo:
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshery/meshery/master/meshes/meshops.proto</code></li>
  <li>Generate code
    <ol>
      <li>Using Go as an example, do the following:
        <ul>
          <li>adding GOPATH to PATH: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">export PATH=$PATH:$GOPATH/bin</code></li>
          <li>install grpc: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go get -u google.golang.org/grpc</code></li>
          <li>install protoc plugin for go: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go get -u github.com/golang/protobuf/protoc-gen-go</code></li>
          <li>Generate Go code: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">protoc -I meshes/ meshes/meshops.proto --go_out=plugins=grpc:./meshes/</code></li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>For other languages, please refer to gRPC.io for language-specific guides.</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
  <li>Implement the service methods and expose the gRPC server on a port of your choice (e.g. 10000).</li>
</ol>

<p>Tip: The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-istio">Meshery Adapter for Istio</a> is a good reference adapter to use as an example of a Meshery Adapter.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
